some random fun dev facts for the day. in both batim/batdr we have an editor tool we just call "T'ing" which in a sentence would be said as "just T through it" this just enters a free roaming camera mode, where it leaves the player behind and the camera can freely fly around anywhere and through walls. you can also go really fast if you hold shift while moving around. when you press T again, it'll place the player exactly where you where seamlessly. this makes for testing specific things super easy and quick if it needs to be tested dozens of times. in batim specifically, we have a tool for speeding up time. which gives hilarious results. but in play mode if you press SHIFT+F it will speed up time super fast, including audio. and we used to use this to do super fast tests where we didn't want to T through anything and allow for sequences to trigger properly. in BLW we had a cheat tool by pressing ~ beside 1 on the keyboard and a menu would appear that gives all kinds of options to cheat, like going to any level, unlocking progression, unlock weapons, add days, or making all items appear right beside the elevator with the click of a button to quickly test a floors end result. in Cage we have, oh sorry we ran out of time here, see you in nightmare run!

content: little update! i'm sure you all heard some buzz that something's coming, and iT's all in good fun, but no there's nothing coming today! that said, i guess it is a good time for some good old fashioned transparency. We're hard at work on a great number Of things for bendy, and while our focus has been on the cage, few tHings came up for us to work on for bendy that's been exciting. being the small team we are, we qUickly pivoted to get that out of the way, and it was a blast! but we're back on cage workiNg away! i've said it before, when the game goes gold on pc we'll let everyone know when it's being ported so you know the time is coming for us to ramp up marketing. now we get super exciteD over here and have been a little trigger happy on announcing things in the past, and we're doing our best to couRse correct that moving forward. so there's one thing i will say from now on when it comes to our gamEs. you'll only ever know "coming soon" or "to be announced" as the Date of a project. the only time we will reveal any kind of timeline, is when the release daTe has been announced. no more years, no more q1, q2, etc. We'd much rather just let you all know that we're working hard, and when the time is right, we'll annOunce actual dates, not vague timelines. so! back to work we go!

summer sale was/is a fantastic success with nearly 400K units sold and just under 24 hours to go. this time around we were doing a little trial and error with some advertising and i’ll keep doing some a/b testing moving forward. one thing i wanted to point out tho was how well the youtube ad did. with a pretty small spend we got over 23M impressions and the ad itself brought in about 1.4M views. it also drove over 550K visits straight to our steam page. we ran the same type of ad on tiktok, facebook, insta and x too but at a much smaller scale. the yt video ended up with well over 11M views tho which was way more than we thought was gonna happen. that means almost 10M of those views were organic. pretty sure the algorithm saw the initial engagement from the ad and just decided to push it more. that was definitely NOT the intention to have an advertisement as our most viewed video, hah! overall it brought in a good chunk of traffic. batdr alone had 224M steam impressions and 4.4M visits to the page. combined with the 90% off deal and steam putting us on the front page it was a solid push. still got a ton to learn when it comes to this stuff but it was a good experiment. we’ll keep testing and improving for the bigger releases so more people can check out some bendy :)

Oversee the content is a better way of saying it. just like we do with everything else, Nightmare Run i have zero hand in developing other than approvals and discussions. same with ports, a few other games, and even the movie, i'm doing nothing other than approvals and discussions. same with meatly, our time is put towards developing the things WE want to make. then we oversee others making the other things we want made. outsourcing it 100% removes some of that control, especially if someone else is financing it. so I'm fine with "outsourcing" so long as we're the ones funding it with 100% creative control. just like we have with nightmare run, the movie, and other games. :)

while i'm still on the hunt for the right partner, i've more or less come to the conclusion that if we want to make a proper series, both a 3d one, and a 2d one, even shorts or any kind of project in that medium, we'd likely want to just fund it and do it ourselves rather than partner with others to take that all on. i'm always going to be open to conversations, but in my hunt i've kind of already determined we gotta do it ourselves unless the absolute perfect partner poofs out of nowhere. i'd also like to add, not a lot of people are willing to take a gamble on bendy, it's a risk, and surely a risk only we're willing to take. but hey, we're the ones with the knowledge of how we lasted almost 10 years and continue to thrive ;)

hah just saw this thread :P i wont give that deep of details but you have to take a lot of thing so to account. we have sold 300,000 copies of batdr. but not every region is $1.99 USD, some regions are far cheaper due to the market. then theres refunds which always happens in droves during sales like this, then you gotta consider the royalties, taxes, yada yada yada. that’s why when you report your sales its easier to say “X units sold” because the math isnt “X units times cost USD” it never is.

budget is a super hard thing to quantify with us. cuz we’re just a couple of dudes making games. doing a thing doesn’t cost money, just our time. so we don’t plan out “it will cost X $ to make a thing” at all. we did that once and it was horrific, but we recovered many years later :P we just kind of go with the flow, and the budget that exists is merely for “how much can we afford to port” and plan around that. and now we’ve added “how much can we afford to market” ;)

no there’s no cost as far as i can remember on console. and steam i think is $100, same with epic games store, but once you’re established, making a new game is free, it’s waived. and all platforms take pretty much the same. steam, nintendo, xbox, playstation all take 30% which is standard and also totally fair considering without their storefronts there would be no 70% to give us ;) other platforms like mobile or epic games store have programs to reduce their take and overall take less in favor of the dev, but for the most part that’s just done to compete against the competition or avoid lawsuits :P i’m fine with 30/70

most studios tend to budget that way. release the game on steam/pc and use those funds to help cover porting costs and release many months later. we put console into the budget from the get go, so fans get it all at once. unfazed by whether or not we will recoup anything or future run way. cuz well… we are the overhead, and it ain’t much to worry about :P

two things here. 1. at some point it’s gotta be a game, so that’s game logic, don’t read into that too much. gameplay is dependant on it, someone can finish it in say 20 “days” and someone else in 478 “days”. so that’s just video game. 2. it’s takes place during events of the dark revival cycle. boris even has visions of events that happened earlier in the cycle. WHEN it all takes place is up to interpretation, as we see boris on the vents of the gent workshop during BATDR (what was he doing there i wonder?). so time goes on but it’s designed to “not matter” for the sake of being a game, while still keeping lore intact.
actually, here’s a good way to look at the series and franchise. Bendy and the Ink Machine IS the prequel to everything that follows.

not a big fan of prequels unless it’s really needed or fits in a good spot. hence why we have games that happen “during events” of other games. prequels tend to kill the mystery, and most of the time destroy built up expectations of what those mysteries are. and when they end up “wrong” to people’s head canon, it can be a complete miss.

batds was a “game” in the truest sense. it did not worry about lore or timelines or cycles. batds was a fun side project that was just a game with no purpose or direction other than just being a bendy game. Lone Wolf rectified that, keeping the series cycles lore more intact.

content: we used to shut the studio down from dec15-jan15 but now it’s like “eh, you don’t have to work, but you can work, but whatever” and we all end up working anyways. but like, we don’t have to? it’s weird.
in fact in cage i have a console that now pops up like old school games and can type commands for cheats.
yeah i have a cheat menu when i press the tilde key on the keyboard.

i had 2 buttons back during development, one would randomly pick a floor. and the other would randomize the level, meaning it would just combine every room type and make a crazy level. those two features kept breaking things, and became more of a derailment to the development i had to call it quits. that said, the randomize floor selection one was the most "working" one that would be a neat feature to add, if ever time existed in an alternate reality.

recently i was in a version of unity from 2018 and 2019 and it blows my mind how i even made games in those versions before. things are so different now, and easier, that those old versions are excruciating to even understand the workflow. i like to stick with unity 6 urp now. i get the workflow, i like the workflow. i don't wanna work in those old versions ever again lol

some small updates batim Switch new pOrt update is now confirMed and slatEd for early january. sorry i couldn’T get it to you all tHis year. blw color correctIon on switch aNd ps is in the works, port team has done a Great job dealIng with the reNdering issues to fix the ultra redness. that’ll be coming soon enough for all 3 games, we’re looKing to do bug fixing on all platforms (pc included) as well as look into being fullY steam deck verified on all games. porT team Has done a great job the last year gettIng our gameS on so many platforms, and We’ll continue to update and finalize them all as best we cAn. it’s been a lot of work, specificallY for the poRt team, it’s time consuming and costly but hopefUlly in 2026 all efforts can be set on moving forward as we fiNish up with our past games. there’s several gameS in the works we gotta focus on, and get started on even. which means back to work on the cage i go. these lost ones aren't gonna chop their own arms off, are they? 🤔... hey that's a good idea!

here’s the workflow btw, from left to right: Monitor 1: Split, left side is communication tools, right side is Repository and windows file explorer Monitor 2: Unity, full monitor Monitor 3: Programming, Unity Game View, Blender, audacity, photoshop, many tools swapped around in full monitor Monitor 4: Split, left side is any type of research in web app. Right side is dedicated to any kind of leisure, so like youtube or whatever this USED to be split between 8 monitors. but 4 is sufficient. yeah i’m still talking about this lol

i also made a really nice tool in unity that when i press Play in the editor it does a full screen mode on another monitor. takes 100% of the screen, so no start menu or nothing. so i can get a nice clear image of what you’d see as a player and not cramped in a unity game view. super handy tool, allows me to use the editor while the full screen is playing somewhere else.

yeah i’m glad to have had the experience of all that, but would never do it again. it was done out of necessity. making a first person game with some combat, was not easy on a mac track pad in a coffee shop. 😅
and a lot of development, most actually, was done one either an airplane, a hotel room, or a coffee shop.
batim was made on a macbook. i’ve since changed my workflow and i cannot go back. 😅

i work on 4 monitors, all across the same row, i’ve tried 3 but my current workflow just needs 4. the two end ones i basically split apps so i can have 2 things going on. basically like having 6 monitors. but i refuse to put a monitor above another. i used to do that when i had 8 monitors. but im down to 4 and id prefer to keep it that way. but i tell you its getting tiring looking left and right 😅 so anyways, im cleaning and rearranging my office and this annoyed me. i have zero solutions. which isnt typical for me. but i’ll just continue to live with it 🙃

if I had to guess, batim would be around 4k hours being in the game doing SOMETHING during development (so not counting time coding or in editor). and if i had to guess batdr, it would be double that.
plenty on the horizon, plenty to manage, plenty to make, lots of bendy. time and patience required. i suck at both of those things. :P
